messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I think fairness means accounting for all three of us, but I don’t know what price or shares would be fair. I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, and C’s agreement matters—she hasn’t agreed yet. What matters most to me is having a stable, independent future. I know B wants money, but not why.

I’d like to use my share to start a dance studio, though I’m not sure what would be fair until we’ve discussed the house and the will together. I know A wants to buy the house, and C hasn’t agreed, so perhaps we can talk through everyone’s needs first.
Yes, I’m open to establishing the market value and discussing any discount openly, with C’s agreement. I don’t know what B needs the money for, so I’d hear her plans before fixing a price.

Yes. Let’s establish the market value first, then discuss any discount and what it means for each of our shares. I haven’t agreed to a discount, and I won’t subsidize A’s purchase. We can take the time to discuss it together.
I’d like to start a small dance studio, but I haven’t worked out a reliable figure yet—it would depend on the space and equipment. I can put together a realistic budget once we know more.
An independent appraisal shared with all three of us sounds sensible. I’m not sure the estate should pay for it; we’d need to agree on that.
An independent appraisal shared with all of us works for me. I can’t commit the estate to paying for it; we should agree on that together.
Yes, I agree to one independent appraisal shared with all three of us. I’d prefer the estate pay for it, if we all think that’s fair.
I’d be willing to have the estate pay, if C agrees too. The cost arrangement should be agreed by all three of us.
Yes, I think it’s fair for the estate to cover the appraisal if all three of us agree. I can’t decide that for the estate alone.
Yes, I agree. One independent appraisal shared with all three of us, paid by the estate, sounds fair. Then we can discuss the discount, shares, and my studio budget.
